'The next RANGER ATTACK ACTION CARD you play this turn gains +1{p}. / Reload / Go again' -- both keywords are printed and fire from the card DB.

MODIFY_NEXT_CARD LOOKS RIGHT AND IS NOT. It queues cost reductions, keyword grants and granted abilities; it has no power grant at all, so `power_mod` there is a parameter nothing reads -- the clause would compile, resolve, and do nothing. audit_params is what caught it.

MODIFY_NEXT_ATTACK carries the power, and the two filters close the gap that made the card queue look wrong for it: ATTACK_TYPE_IN Action excludes a weapon activation, which is the only way the attack queue could be consumed by something that was not played as a card, and ATTACK_CLASS_IN is the Ranger half. Dropping either widens the card.
